lrps.title: Français (Immersion) - Grade 1 French Immersion Excellence
lrps.subject: Français (Immersion)
lrps.description: A comprehensive French language arts program developing emergent literacy through systematic phonological awareness, high-frequency word mastery, guided reading progressions, and authentic writing experiences. Integrates oral communication, cultural identity, and joyful engagement with French literature.
lrps.goals:
SPECIFIC MEASURABLE LEARNING GOALS:
• Students will decode CVC words in French with 90% accuracy by December
• Students will recognize 50 high-frequency French words automatically by March  
• Students will read Level C French texts independently by June
• Students will write 3-sentence stories using emergent spelling by April
• Students will participate in 5-minute French conversations using complete sentences by May
• Students will demonstrate comprehension through retelling with 80% accuracy
• Students will identify all French phonemes and graphemes by February
• Students will use 200+ French vocabulary words in context by year end

lrps.assessmentOverview:
COMPREHENSIVE ASSESSMENT STRATEGY:

FORMATIVE ASSESSMENT (Daily/Weekly):
• Running Records: PM Benchmarks French (bi-weekly) with error analysis
• Phonics Quick-Checks: Weekly systematic phoneme assessment
• Oral Language Sampling: Monthly video recordings with rubrics
• Interactive Writing Observations: Daily anecdotal notes
• Reading Response Discussions: Participation tracking charts
• Word Work Checks: Weekly sight word assessments

SUMMATIVE ASSESSMENT (Monthly/Term):
• Portfolio Conferences: Student self-selected best work
• Performance Tasks: Storytelling, readers theatre, puppet shows
• Writing Samples: Monthly collection (narrative, informational, opinion)
• French Literacy Skills Checklist: Comprehensive monthly review
• Reading Level Assessments: GB+ or PM Benchmarks monthly
• Oral Communication Rubrics: Formal presentations quarterly

lrps.subject: Mathématiques
lrps.description: A hands-on, inquiry-based mathematics program building number sense to 100, operational fluency, pattern recognition, spatial reasoning, and problem-solving strategies through concrete-pictorial-abstract progressions aligned with current research in mathematical cognition.
lrps.goals:
SPECIFIC MEASURABLE LEARNING GOALS:
• Students will count to 100 by 1s, 2s, 5s, and 10s with 95% accuracy
• Students will solve addition problems to 20 using 3+ strategies
• Students will solve subtraction problems to 20 using 3+ strategies  
• Students will identify, create, and extend AB, ABC, AAB, and AABB patterns
• Students will name and describe 8 2D shapes and 5 3D solids in French
• Students will measure using non-standard units with 90% accuracy
• Students will collect, organize, and interpret data in 3 different ways
• Students will solve word problems using drawing, acting out, or manipulatives
• Students will explain mathematical thinking orally in French
• Students will recognize number patterns and relationships to 100

• Students will observe and document 10 seasonal changes using scientific drawings
• Students will classify 20 objects as living/non-living with 90% accuracy
• Students will identify 5 basic needs of living things through investigation
• Students will name 3 energy sources in their daily environment
• Students will predict outcomes of 5 simple experiments with reasoning
• Students will use 30 French science vocabulary words in context
• Students will ask testable questions about natural phenomena
• Students will record observations using pictures, numbers, and words
• Students will identify 5 ways humans impact the environment
• Students will demonstrate 10 safety procedures in science activities

ESSENTIAL QUESTIONS (Concrete & Observable):
• Qu'est-ce qui vit? (What is alive?)
• Que voit-on dehors? (What do we see outside?)
• Comment ça change? (How does it change?)
• D'où vient l'énergie? (Where does energy come from?)
• Comment on sait? (How do we know?)
• Pourquoi c'est important? (Why does it matter?)

SAFETY PROTOCOLS (MANDATORY):
• Outdoor supervision ratio: 1:8 maximum
• Hand washing before/after all investigations
• No tasting without explicit permission
• Safety goggles for any splashing activities
• Allergy awareness for all nature materials
• Emergency procedures posted and practiced
• First aid kit accessibility verified daily
• Weather safety guidelines followed

FORMATIVE ASSESSMENT (Daily/Weekly):
• Science journals with dated observations
• Photo documentation of investigations
• "I Notice, I Wonder" charts
• Prediction vs. outcome recordings
• Scientific drawing progression portfolios
• Oral explanations in French
• Safety procedure demonstrations

SUMMATIVE ASSESSMENT (Unit/Term):
• Investigation projects with presentations
• Living/non-living sorting assessments
• Seasonal change documentation books
• Energy use home audits
• Science fair projects (simplified)
• Nature collection classifications

lrps.goals:

• Students will identify and name 5 basic emotions using emoji scales by December
• Students will demonstrate 3 calm-down strategies independently by March
• Students will practice 10 personal hygiene habits correctly with 90% consistency
• Students will identify 5 trusted adults in their safety network
• Students will use 4 conflict resolution steps with peer support
• Students will recognize 8 body safety rules and boundaries
• Students will demonstrate kindness in 95% of peer interactions
• Students will identify healthy vs unhealthy foods with 85% accuracy
• Students will participate in 15 minutes of physical activity daily
• Students will express personal strengths and challenges appropriately
